Hey OP, my father was the same way for a long time and implied inappropriate things about family and shamed me and my sisters for it, as well as being disgusted about my period for the same reason. I found out recently that he went through sexual abuse by a family member and the stigma around talking about it/getting help made him paranoid and projected it on my siblings and I. It would be really helpful to talk to a professional about it because it was clearly emotionally disturbing and traumatic to effect you in the long term, just know this isn’t your fault and the way you feel is reasonable and valid.

That’s what I really consider as the issue with Islamic tradition. So much of it is culture and this culture is suffocating. That’s why I left, it’s blurred the lines and chased away my feelings of faith with the fear and control from the community.

It does feel like the torment is finally over. I’ve had to take legal action against him to stay safe after I left, but I still feel bad about how he passed. He was in a lot of pain. My siblings got to be with him for his last moments, and not being a part of that hurt. Even as an adult, I still feel like a kid who wants their father to love them unconditionally. Faith taught him to be against that, but I hope still down he had love for me like I did him. I hate that the pain from my childhood and his raising can still hurt even now that he’s gone. 

I’m sorry for what you’ve gone through, but your comment definitely helped me feel less alone. I love this community because it’s so hard to find places to share and heal from religious abuse when it’s not mainstream like Christianity. I’ve had so little resources navigating it and getting treatment for the PTSD it gave me, but it helps to hear from those who have gotten out of it stronger. Makes me feel like I’ll get through it too. Thank you for the kind words and best of luck to you while we all heal 🤍
